texts: The peacock spreads his splendid tail, yet the gossips pick at the shabby feet beneath; let me praise rather than pick.
My sister-in-law dresses up like a peacock for parties, then spends the whole evening picking apart other women's outfits.
peacock, gossip, faults
doha about backbiting w a peacock, thx

I'd like a doha that shows that the peacock displays his splendid feathers but hides his ugly feet, so whoever gossips about the faults of others should first look at his own flaws before opening his mouth.
Someone told the neighbours I am stingy and it felt like being hit by a stone; I do not know whether to answer or stay quiet.
doha on ppl who throw stones at others with gossip
stone, backbiting
Compose a doha showing that a person who hurls stones of slander at others should remember his own life is full of cracks, so it is better to stay quiet than to cast stones at another's good name.
Slander is thrown like a stone at a good name, and the thrower's own hand grows weary and bloodied.

Please write a doha explaining that gossip is like the oil press that crushes a person's reputation drop by drop, and whoever feeds the press with rumours will finally find himself pressed under it too.
The oil press yields only after crushing the grain; so does a rumour crush a good name before any truth appears.
oil press, gossip
doha with an oil press about how rumours squeeze people
The women at the oil press spend every afternoon talking about who married whom and who is cheating whom; I stay away.
fly, tongue, gossip
doha abt how the tongue goes where a fly goes: to dirt, always finding faults
The fly seeks the wound and the tongue seeks the fault; both leave the healthy untouched but filth behind.

Could you write a couplet saying that a fly ignores the fresh body and settles on the sore, just as a gossiping tongue passes by every virtue and lands only on faults, thereby infecting itself with filth.
My colleague's tongue works like a fly, ignoring all my good work and settling on the one mistake I made last month.
A priest in our town spends more time criticising others than praying, and I wonder if he sees his own faults at all.
doha about a priest who bad-mouths everyone
The priest preaches purity from the pulpit but keeps a ledger of his neighbours' sins; whose book is truly full of stains?

Looking for a verse about how a priest who spends his days finding fault with others has forgotten the one fault he should be correcting, namely his own, and that real piety begins with looking inward.
priest, slander
critic, keep him near
My harshest critic at work tells me every mistake I make, and strangely I have never improved faster than this year.
doha on how a critic is actually helpful, keep him close
Keep the fault-finder close, for he washes the mind clean with no soap and no water.

Please give me a doha explaining that the person who points out my mistakes is more useful than a flatterer, and I should keep him near me, since he cleans my character without the need for soap or water.
Whenever the aunties meet, they tear apart other families' reputations like a sheet in the wind, and later they are the ones whose own pearls are fake.
doha abt gossip that ruins a pearl of a reputation, cloth sheet vibes
Make me a couplet showing how slander tears the clean cloth sheet of a person's good name which took years to weave, and the rumour-monger can never repair it even if he offers a pearl in apology.
cloth sheet, pearl, rumours
A pearl takes years to form but a rumour can stain the cloth sheet of a name in a single evening.

Compose a doha showing that one who burns with envy and slanders sandalwood-like saints only fans a fire that consumes himself, while the sandalwood goes on giving fragrance to even the axe that cuts it.
doha on sandalwood who stays fragrant despite slander, fire everywhere
sandalwood, fire, slander
People in my village spread nasty stories about the sandalwood seller out of envy, and he just keeps smiling while the fire of jealousy eats them.
Sandalwood gives fragrance to the very axe that fells it; the slanderer's fire consumes only himself.
doha for a traveler who hears gossip about himself in every town
traveler, gossip
As a traveler passing through new towns I notice every village loves to talk about its neighbours behind their backs.
The traveler leaves the town but the gossip stays; wise is he who carries no rumour in his bag.
Give me a doha telling that a traveler on the road of life who stops to criticise every person he meets will reach nowhere, since fault-finding is a heavy burden that slows even the swiftest feet.
Let the lamp of kindness light my words, and let no stain of slander fall on another's name.
lamp, no fault-finding
By the lamp last night my mother-in-law complained about everyone in the family, and I silently wondered what she said about me.
Can you put into a doha the idea that a lamp lights its surroundings but cannot see the darkness at its base, just as a gossip sees every fault in others but never the faults in his own life.
doha on lamp - cant see own darkness while pointing out others

Compose a doha about how the slanderer carries the sins of the one he criticises and gives away his own good deeds, so that the one slandered becomes cleaner while the slanderer slowly loses everything he had.
A friend of mine spent a whole year spreading rumours about me, and today he has none left to trust him while I am calm.
slander, loses all
doha on ppl who talk bad about me, I know its karma
Whoever speaks ill of another empties his own store of virtue into the hands of the one he abused.
The washerman at the water says the gossip of the village is dirtier than anything he washes, and flies of rumour settle on every roof.
washerman, fly, gossip
doha with a washerman and a fly, about dirty talk
The washerman can cleanse any garment, but who will wash the mind that, like a fly, settles on every fault?
I'd like a doha that shows that a washerman can clean the dirtiest garment but cannot clean the mind of a gossip, who like a fly always seeks out the filth in others and carries it about.
Seek the faults of none, and your own will shrink; the one who looks outward for flaws walks blindly past himself.

Could you write a couplet saying that those who spend their time talking about the weaknesses of others never find time to improve themselves, and thus remain exactly where they started, while others quietly grow beyond them.
My father-in-law has never in thirty years said a good word about anyone, and he is the loneliest man in the family.
doha about gossiping behind ppl's backs
backbiting hurts you
Looking for a verse about how the chakor bird looks only skyward and ignores all else, whereas a cleric who spends his time slandering rivals has no vision at all, and his preaching is full of venom.
The chakor gazes skyward with love, while the cleric mutters of others' sins; which one is closer to God?
The cleric in our street keeps a list of everyone's wrongdoing but never looks at his own; the chakor I keep sings sweeter than he preaches.
doha abt a cleric who talks badly about everybody
chakor, cleric, gossip
mirror, forehead mark, faults

Please give me a doha explaining that a person with a bright forehead mark who tells everyone others' mistakes should first look in the mirror, because there he will find the one person whose faults he has never counted.
Hold up the mirror to yourself before you hold up the finger to another; the forehead mark will not hide what it shows.
My neighbour wears a big forehead mark and criticises every girl on our street, though her own daughter has never once looked her in the mirror's eye.
doha about looking in the mirror before judging others, with tilak
stop judging others

Make me a couplet showing how the person who is always busy pointing out the faults of others will never see how his own life has gone astray, and that gentle silence is better than a clever criticism.
doha on gossiping, what goes around comes around
The finger that points at another curls three back toward the pointer; remember this, O hasty judge.
I caught myself at the family gathering whispering about my cousin's divorce, and the shame stayed with me all week.
Compose a doha about a woman at the market who stitches a rumour with a needle of sharp words, sewing a false story into a good family's name, which can never be unpicked however much she regrets it.
The needle of sharp words stitches a false story into a good name, and no hand can ever unpick it.
doha on a market gossip with her needle-sharp comments
needle, market, rumours
At the market yesterday a woman sewed a false story about my family out of nothing, and the whole street believes her.
doha on a weaver, a well and gossip, thx

Give me a doha telling that the weaver at his loom has no time to slander anyone, for his hands are busy with honest work, while those gathered idly at the well fill the air with tales about their neighbours.
loom, well, gossip
The weaver's loom hums with honest labour, while at the well the idle draw only rumours.
The women at our well talk of others all morning, and the weaver nearby only works at his loom; I know who is happier.
Whoever seeks the faults of others finds his own mind full of dust; let me turn the lens inward and sweep.
Can you put into a doha the idea that the person who is full of criticism for others should first search his own life, because when the searcher looks inside he finds no one worse than himself.
find your own flaws
I went looking for who was most selfish at our family gathering and ended up realising it was me.
doha: looked for bad ppl, found myself
doha on palace gossip, courtiers love to tear each other down
My cousin works at a grand palace hotel and says the staff talk behind everyone's back all day, even about the owners.
palace, courtiers, slander
In the palace the courtiers murmur, each sharpening a barb of words for the other's back.
I'd like a doha that shows that gossip thrives in the courts of kings, where flatterers praise to the face and slander behind the back, and that a wise man keeps away from both kinds of talk.
scales, fair judgment
When my friends judged my brother without hearing his side, I felt as though the scales were weighted against him from the start.
Weigh your own deeds on the scales before you weigh another, and slander will fall silent.
doha on weighing others fairly with scales instead of backbiting

Could you write a couplet saying that a person who sits with scales to weigh others' faults should first weigh himself, and the weights will show he is far lighter than he thinks and has no right to criticise.
doha on a weaver and an elephant, the critics bark but u keep walking
loom, elephant, critics
They gossip about my work like dogs barking at an elephant, while I quietly continue at my loom, hoping it will pass.

Compose a doha showing that the elephant walks on while dogs bark at it, just as the weaver at his loom goes on working, ignoring the critics, because the truth of his work will speak louder than any rumour.
The elephant walks on and the barking falls behind; the loom clacks on as the critics fade.

Looking for a verse about how at the crossroads of every town the pearl of a person's name is bargained over by gossips, and he who protects his silence preserves it, while loose talk loses it for good.
doha: crossroads gossip kills pearls (reputations) lol
At the crossroads outside our village, the men decide each evening whose reputation to pull apart, and that pearl of trust is slowly lost.
At the crossroads the gossips gather and sell a pearl for a story; the poor victim never knows his loss.
crossroads, pearl, rumour
speak no ill
Write a doha reminding me that speaking ill of others, even when I am hurt, only brings sorrow in the end, and that the better path is to forgive silently and let time reveal the truth.
Let no word of blame pass your lips, for blame returns like an echo to its source.
My roommate has been telling people lies about me for months, and I want to stay dignified and not retaliate.
doha for staying quiet when someone badmouths u
They whisper behind my back; let them, for each whisper washes me cleaner than any bath.
doha on enjoying having haters, they clean my faults for free
A colleague keeps spreading small rumours about me, and I am learning to thank him for the lessons.
let critics talk
Please give me a doha explaining that people who slander me are doing me a favour, because they carry my sins away and make my character stronger, so I should not fight them but be grateful.
ok so, doha about ppl who gossip behind ur back lol
The backbiter sleeps in the company of his own worries, while the slandered one sleeps like a child.
Make me a couplet showing how those who spend their evenings picking apart others' lives are poor in their own, and that a quiet life of silent work earns more respect than a clever mocking wit.
gossip empties you
My cousin keeps score of everybody's failures at family functions, and I am noticing nobody invites her to dinners anymore.
Praise the good you see, be silent on the rest, and your name will bloom unharmed by any envy.
criticise not, praise
Write a doha reminding us that for each fault we find in another we should find three good qualities, since the person who seeks only flaws ends up with a heavy heart and an empty circle of friends.
doha on focusing on others' good rather than bad
My mother taught me that if I have nothing nice to say about a person I should say nothing, and it has served me fine.
The thread of gossip tangles all who hold it; cut it early, before it ties a whole village together in knots.
doha on gossip being a thread that knots everyone up
Give me a doha telling that a thread of gossip begins thin and harmless but grows and knots until it chokes an entire community, so the wise one must cut it at the very first pull.
One small remark by my aunt got passed from person to person like a thread, and by evening three families were quarrelling.
thread of rumour
Write a doha about how the furnace of jealousy makes a man steal good names the way a thief steals purses at night, yet the stolen reputation melts in his hands and leaves only soot behind.
The slanderer is a thief who steals a good name in the dark, and the furnace of shame awaits him at dawn.
doha on slandering as stealing, furnace and thief
The man who spread lies about my business once sat by the blacksmith's furnace and swore he was honest; everyone knows he is a thief of names.
furnace, thief, slander
Can you put into a doha the idea that a fly leaves the sweet food and sits on the sore, just as a faultfinder ignores all the good in a person and buzzes around the one flaw forever.
doha about faultfinders and flies
My colleagues ignore all my years of hard work and gossip like flies only about the one mistake I made.
fly, faultfinder
The fly forsakes the feast to find the wound; so the gossip skips the virtue and seeks the stain.
The lion walks his path unbothered by the oil press of gossip grinding behind him.
doha w a lion and an oil press, ignoring critics
People crush my reputation at the oil press every day, but I walk like a lion and do not turn to look back.
lion, oil press, critics
I'd like a doha that shows that a lion pays no attention to the barking behind him, just as a person of strength pays no attention to rumours, which like the oil press grind only the weak who listen.
A grindstone grinds grain, a stone of slander grinds a name; neither heeds the cries of the one beneath.
grindstone, stone, slander
The women at our grindstone chat about the stone-hearted neighbour all day, grinding down her name more than the wheat.
doha on a grindstone and a stone, gossip grinding ppl down

Could you write a couplet saying that gossip is a heavy grindstone which crushes the good name of the poor and weak, while the one who turns it carries the dust of his own cruelty on his hands till death.
doha for my mum who spends all day on the phone talking bad about others
Compose a doha that says one who loves to listen to criticism of others is as guilty as the one who speaks it, so refusing to listen is as important as refusing to speak when slander is in the air.
don't listen to gossip
When my colleagues began whispering about the new girl at lunch, I got up and left, and I felt oddly proud of myself.
Close both ears to calumny, as you would shut your mouth to it; the listener shares the sin of the speaker.
The thread of reputation is spun over years, and cut by a rumour; the bier waits to see which is longer.
thread, bier, rumour
Even at my uncle's bier, people whispered about his old debts, as if one thread of gossip could undo a lifetime.
Looking for a verse about how a person's good name is a long thread spun over a lifetime, which slander can cut in one breath, and that nothing can mend it even when the bier is carried out.
doha on rumours that last till the bier, thread of a name
Please give me a doha explaining that a person who finds fault with others from a high seat is like a man sawing his own perch, because the cruel judgments he gives will one day be applied to him.
judge not, fall not
He who judges from a high seat will one day sit on the lowest; remember the judge shall be judged.
My manager criticised my work harshly in front of everyone, then lost his own job for the same mistake the following month.
doha on karma for people who judge others
My neighbour compares herself to a peacock and gossips that I am plain; I wonder if her beauty is only in her feathers.
doha on a peacock who badmouths others
The peacock mocks the plain bird, forgetting his own scream when the rain begins.
Make me a couplet showing how a peacock may boast of his beautiful feathers and mock others, but his voice is harsh and he is judged by it, so pride in looks should not become a reason to slander.
peacock, mocking
doha on the people who throw a stone at ur name and run
Could you write a couplet about the person who throws a stone at another's reputation and hides his hand, noting that the stone always lands back on him in the end, usually when he least expects it?
The stone of slander flies from a hidden hand, but gravity brings it back to the thrower's brow.
Someone has been dropping nasty comments about me online and then running away, and I would like to answer with dignity instead of stones.
stone, slander, silence
rainbird doha: gossip is a thirst that never ends
The rainbird waits for one pure drop; the slanderer drinks the muddy talk of every passerby and is never full.
The rainbird outside our window waits patiently for the first drops, unlike my nosy neighbour who cannot wait to share every bit of news about others.
rainbird, idle gossip
Write me a doha about how the rainbird thirsts only for pure rain and refuses stagnant water, so a person of virtue should refuse to drink in the muddy gossip of the crowd and keep his ears clean.
I'd like a doha in which salt in a wound stands for slander, because a cruel remark made to a person already in pain stings far worse, and only gentle silence can stop the wound from festering.
doha on gossip being salt on a wound lol
Slander is salt upon the open wound; the kind soul leaves the sufferer's sore untouched.
After my divorce, people kept adding salt to my wound by whispering about my faults at every wedding I attended.
salt, slander, wounds
My mother-in-law has a new theory every week about why our neighbour's marriage failed, and I am tired of hearing it.
doha: why do ppl love talking about others' lives so much
Idle minds gather rumours as lonely ones gather echoes; the busy soul has no leisure for either.
idle talk, empty minds
Compose a doha explaining that the person who always has a story about other people's failings is hiding his own emptiness, and that a mind full of its own work has no time for gossip.
slander brings sorrow
The tale that wounds another is a sapling of sorrow growing in the sower's own field.
doha on karma of badmouthing ppl
The friend who ruined my name at college is now the one nobody trusts, and I feel strangely sad rather than glad.
I'd like a doha that says speaking ill of others may bring a moment of pleasure but plants a long-lasting regret, and that those who speak with malice eventually find themselves at the receiving end.
We walked through the forest to the bridge, and my companions spent the whole way mocking the one who had stayed behind, which spoiled the hike for me.
forest, bridge, gossip
On the bridge through the forest of life, the one who stops to mock the stragglers never reaches the far side.
Please give me a doha about how a bridge connects two banks, but gossip is a bridge burned with jealousy, and a forest of friendships can be lost when envy drives people to speak against each other.
doha w forest and bridge about badmouthing friends
The moon shows its spots to all and still shines on; the moneylender counts others' sins but cannot count his own.
The moneylender in our town has a long ledger of everyone's faults, but under the moon at night he alone cannot sleep.
moon, moneylender, faultfinding

Looking for a couplet about how the moon bears its dark spots without complaint and gives its cool light to all, while a moneylender counts the debts of others' reputations and finds himself poor in peace.
doha on moneylender bad-mouthing ppl, moon as example of grace
The old man with the one-string lute at our station gets mocked for his out-of-tune music, as moths are mocked for circling the glare, yet he plays on and never complains.
Looking for a doha with a one-string lute and a moth, where the moth is drawn to the glare of slander and gets scorched, while the lute plays on, humbly unaffected by the noise of critics.
The moth is drawn to the glare of idle talk and burns, while the lone lute plays on, untouched by blame.
lute, moth, gossip
doha w ektara and moth, critics burn themselves

Can you write a doha showing that a leaf blown by the wind is carried wherever rumour goes, and that those who spread thorny words are pricked themselves before the leaf has settled, so one must speak with care?
A leaf that follows every breeze is lost; a word that follows every rumour is thorny, and wounds the hand that sowed it.
doha on leaf and thorn, gossip blows everywhere and hurts
leaf, thorn, gossip
A rumour about me went through the town like a leaf in the wind, and a thorn of it still stays with me.
can u write a doha on staying away from fault finders
My uncle spent his retirement telling everyone what they did wrong in their lives, and now no one visits him, not even his own children.
critic, silence, peace
Better to dwell alone than in the company of the slanderer, who feeds on the faults of his friends.
Write me a doha explaining that those who live to find faults in others are never happy, because their eyes see only what is wrong, and the world becomes smaller and darker the longer they look.
cloud, door, gossip

Make me a couplet showing that gossip is a dark cloud over the door of a household, bringing storms of quarrel, and the wise man keeps his door closed against such visitors and speaks kindly of others.
A cloud of rumour gathers at the neighbour's door, and the storm that follows rains on every roof.
A bit of idle talk drifted like a cloud into the neighbour's door and by night three families were in an uproar.
doha on gossip clouds at the doorstep, how to keep out
The furnace of envy glows on a bed of sand, and the one who fans it finds his own reputation turn to dust.
doha on a furnace in the sand, jealous ppl and gossip
furnace, sand, backbiting
I'd like a doha showing that slander is built on sand and cannot last, however hot the furnace of envy that forged it, because truth in the end washes away such flimsy constructions without a trace.
Some local envious people forged lies about me in their furnace of jealousy, but they were all built on sand and fell away within a month.
keep your critic near
Could you write a doha saying that I should keep the one who criticises me always close, because he cleans my faults without soap or water, while the flatterer leaves me dirty and proud?
doha on appreciating ur critics, they help u improve
My harshest critic is my old teacher, and the more she scolds me the more I grow; I want to thank her in verse.
Build a hut beside the one who finds your faults, and he will cleanse you daily without soap or water.
Even a skeleton in a museum keeps silent about the rest of us, while we spend our living days dissecting each other's lives.
skeleton, silence, gossip
doha on how ppl gossip while we all end up as skeletons
The skeleton judges nobody; living men judge each other, and soon enough join the quiet company of bones.
Compose a doha showing that all the slander and gossip we engage in will end when we are nothing more than a skeleton, so we ought to spend our short time on kindness and mutual respect.
